provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1862 opening word carried by an ornamental initial; the scan's recogniser loses it (target opens intercessio); recogniser damage, same word: target reads quesumus domine beati n abbatis, the 1862 layer reads qusesumus d mine bedti x abbdtis; recogniser damage, same word: target reads meritis, the 1862 layer reads msritis; recogniser damage, same word: target reads ualemus, the 1862 layer reads ual mus; recogniser damage, letterforms inferred rather than read: target reads assequamur, the 1862 layer reads assequdmur i er d minum; conclusion length: the 1862 prints the short printed cue where the 1962 writes the conclusion out. Corroboration: 1922 Mame, artifact PDF p. 910 (printed p. 32* of the Commune Sanctorum); read from the page's word bounding boxes, reflowed column by column; reading: Siebia nos, quésumus, Domine, beati N. Abbatis comméndet ut, quod nostris méritis non valémus, ejus patrocinio assequamur. Per Doéminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fillum tuum, qui tecum vivit.. Recorded limitation: Found in the 1862's own Missa pro Abbatibus, in the Commune Sanctorum run, printing the placeholder (the layer renders it X.). The 1862's ornamental initial destroys the opening word, and the 1862 abbreviates the conclusion. Target reading settled on the CMAA facsimile page image at 450 dpi; the crops read are kept in .scratch/backfill/commons-2/work/img. Not checked: the 1862's own page images, which this repository holds only for printed pp. [31], [32], [37] and [52]-[56].
